analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds, at head lines 757-765, a paragraph describing how streamed `auto` tool calls span several `inference_response_chunk` frames. It sits under the chunk table that includes `encrypted_data`, ahead of the `inference_complete` section. The paragraph says streamed tool calls share one `index`, with the first chunk carrying `id`, `type`, `function.name` and empty `function.arguments`, and later chunks carrying only `index` plus `function.arguments` fragments, which consumers concatenate by `index`. I examined it against the threat model and found no source or code change. There is no change to encryption (T-008), authorization, attestation (TB-009, TB-011), the prefix-cache storage tier (T-041), routing or billing. The text describes the OpenAI-compatible delta format and does not alter the per-chunk encryption contract. The existing base text still says `data` is empty when E2E encryption is active, and the new paragraph does not contradict that. The paragraph cites `libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMServer/Runtime/MLXOpenAIService.swift` (`streamChatCompletionFrames`) and `../architecture/inference.md#streamed-auto-tool-calls`. Neither file is in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that the described behavior exists, or that the fragments are encrypted rather than sent in plaintext. This is a documentation-accuracy question for whoever reviews the matching source change, not a finding here. Consumers are adversarial per the model, so fragment reassembly is consumer-side, which is fine. No threat model update is needed from this doc-only change.
